title: NRI Achievers Awards 2026 in Singapore Honors 24 Indian Diaspora Leaders Across Eight Countries
excerpt: The 5th edition of the NRI Achievers Awards recognized Indian-origin professionals from the US, UK, Australia, Singapore, and beyond for contributions spanning AI, healthcare, engineering, and entrepreneurship.
body:
• The 5th edition of the NRI Achievers Awards 2026 honored 24 Indian diaspora professionals at The St. Regis Singapore on July 31, recognizing achievements across technology, healthcare, research, and business.
  • UK-based AI professional Manohar Reddy received the Global Achievement in Artificial Intelligence & Data Science award, one of several technology-focused recognitions at the ceremony.
  • Winners represented eight countries including the US, UK, Australia, Singapore, New Zealand, UAE, Zambia, and Nigeria, spanning fields from genomic research to immigration law.
  • The awards have grown from their Mumbai origins to international editions in Dubai, London, and now Singapore.

Singapore Ceremony Marks Global Expansion

The NRI Achievers Awards held its 5th annual ceremony at The St. Regis Singapore on July 31, 2026, honoring 24 Indian-origin professionals for contributions across technology, healthcare, scientific research, business leadership, and community service. The Singapore edition marked the latest step in the awards' expansion from domestic origins to an international platform spanning three continents.

Organized by Eventinity Ventures, the ceremony brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs, policymakers, diplomats, and members of the Indian diaspora. Johnson Paul, Director of Group Strategy and Business Development at Meinhardt Singapore, attended as chief guest and commended the awardees for their role in driving innovation and economic growth globally.

Previous editions were held at Radisson Blu London and Hilton London Wembley, with the awards originating in Mumbai and Dubai before expanding to international venues.

Technology and AI Dominate the Honors

Technology professionals figured prominently among the 2026 honorees. UK-based Manohar Reddy received the Global Achievement in Artificial Intelligence & Data Science award, according to reports in the European Sun Times and Telugu Times. The recognition was one of several AI and technology-focused awards at the ceremony.

Dr. Anjulika Salhan, also based in the United Kingdom, was honored for Global Excellence in AI-Driven FinTech Innovation. Salhan was previously recognized at the 2025 NRI Achievers Awards in London. Singapore-based Mukundan A.P. received the Global Distinguished Leadership in AI & Data Science award, while Satyam Sheth earned recognition for Global Leadership in Cloud Computing & Technology Innovation.

Other technology winners included Saurabh Jain (UK) for Digital Transformation & AI Leadership, Vinay Gulati (UK) for Technology Leadership & Business Transformation, and Abhishek Marla (Singapore) for Media, Technology & Content-Commerce Innovation.

Healthcare and Research Recognized

The ceremony also highlighted contributions in healthcare and scientific research. Dr. Tushar B. Patel of the United States received the Global Leadership in Public Health & Community Healthcare award, a recognition highlighted by HI India and The Indian Eye in their coverage.

Australia-based Rudrarup Bhattacharjee was honored for Global Leadership in Medical Research & Genomic Innovation, while Dr. Sivanesan Dakshanamurthy of the United States received the Global Impact Award for Science, Health & Innovation. Dr. Shabhihul Hassan, based in Nigeria, received a Lifetime Achievement recognition for Healthcare, Humanitarian Service & Nation Building.

"The contributions of the Indian diaspora in driving innovation, economic growth, and social development across the world deserve recognition."

— Johnson Paul, Director, Meinhardt Singapore, Chief Guest

Winners Span Eight Countries

The 24 honorees represented eight countries across five continents. The United Kingdom had the largest representation with six winners, followed by Australia and Singapore with four each, and the United States with three. New Zealand contributed two honorees — Janesh Kharbanda for entrepreneurship and hospitality, and Vinay Donthineni for business development and education leadership.

Beyond the established diaspora hubs, the awards also recognized professionals in Zambia and Nigeria. Dr. Narendra Bhati (Zambia) received the Global Excellence in Industrial Entrepreneurship & Social Impact award, and Dr. Naresh Gupta (Australia) earned a Lifetime Achievement recognition in Civil Engineering & Infrastructure.

Yumnam Sanajaoba of Singapore was notably recognized for Global Business Leadership with Impact on Northeast India, and Rashpal Singh of the United Kingdom was honored for excellence in UK Immigration & Legal Advisory — reflecting the breadth of fields represented.

A Growing Platform

The NRI Achievers Awards has evolved from a single domestic event to an international recognition platform that rotates between global cities. The Singapore edition's focus on technology professionals — with nearly a third of awards going to AI, data science, and digital transformation leaders — reflects the outsized role Indian-origin professionals play in the global tech industry.

With editions now spanning Mumbai, Dubai, London, and Singapore, the awards have positioned themselves as a circuit for recognizing Indian diaspora achievement beyond the more established platforms like the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman.
